blasian117: "You're late," said the corporal when Hugo Blasian arrived on Day 9. "Everyone's late. Get a spade."
eddholmesss: On the way to R-F18, Tobias "Whistle" Eddholmesss tried to memorise every turn. By the dugout door, he was simply glad someone else knew the way.

Orders came through: Tobias "Whistle" Eddholmesss is a sniper now. He handed in his old kit and kept only a bullet that missed him. The report confirmed the Concord victory at Verdel Ridge. Tobias "Whistle" Eddholmesss folded the paper so the headline stayed on the outside.
Tobias "Whistle" Eddholmesss noticed regular flashes from a crack in an old stone wall. The position looks obvious enough to make him suspicious.

Tobias "Whistle" Eddholmesss watched a crack in an old stone wall through another shift. The flash returns at the same angle, even when nothing else moves. Mail came up the line with a letter for Tobias "Whistle" Eddholmesss. Tobias "Whistle" Eddholmesss read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Tobias "Whistle" Eddholmesss drew a line on the bench to settle an argument about space. Everyone obeyed it until the broadest man returned from duty. Day 6. Hill 304 fell to the Hegemony. Tobias "Whistle" Eddholmesss watched their flag go up on the heights and dug his trench a little deeper.
A clear shot from R-F18. Tobias "Whistle" Eddholmesss gravely wounded Jakub "Brick" Ingfan and slid back down below the parapet.
A second observer helped Tobias "Whistle" Eddholmesss confirm the trick: a piece of glass, placed to draw fire. The real watching point must be elsewhere.
A round went through Tobias "Whistle" Eddholmesss's water bottle and into his thigh, but not far. He is more upset about the water. Shot by Clement Wanter of the Hegemony (@wanter_cz).
Tobias "Whistle" Eddholmesss rejoined the squad at R-F18. Someone had written his name on the wall with 'still alive' under it. He left it there.
egga15627: On Day 9 Gustav Egga took a post at R-C10 that had been empty for two nights. He did not ask why. He shares cigarettes but never smokes, and the men liked him for it. Gustav Egga transferred to the machine gunners. The men in R-C10 said they would miss him. He is only three dugouts away.
evie.sh207: Tobias "Hollow" Evie reported to T-F8 with a rosary of rough beads sewn into his tunic lining. The sergeant pretended not to notice.
fade_data35: The draft reached Q-F15 on Day 9. Hugo "Crow" Data was shown which board tipped, which roof leaked and which promises to ignore.
falloutvam: Benedikt Falloutvam arrived at R-S2 with a carefully folded uniform. The first low beam ruined the cap; the first puddle ruined the rest.
Benedikt Falloutvam traded a cigarette for a pinch of salt. Supper improved. The argument about the exchange rate did not.
harry_betts91774: "You're late," said the corporal when Valentin Betts arrived on Day 6. "Everyone's late. Get a spade."
Valentin Betts and Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas made a pact on sentry tonight: whoever gets home first visits the other's family. They shook on it.
Valentin Betts was halfway through a story when his listener fell asleep. He counted that as a success.
Valentin Betts sang under his breath on sentry. Across the wire, very quietly, somebody sang the next line.
Across the wire at Verdel Ridge, Arno Dick of the Hegemony held up a sign: 'How is your coffee?' Valentin Betts of the Concord held up a sign back: 'Worse than yours.'
jackal.raf: Nobody asked Florian "Button" Raf why he came. Nobody in R-C9 asks that. He was handed a spade before he was handed a rifle.
masis_xiii: Bastian Xiii signed the papers with a steady hand. The trench at R-F13 took him in like it takes everyone: without a word.
Bastian Xiii answered the first call, number 25 on the rolls. Somebody chalked the number on his helmet. It has not washed off yet.
A clear sky. Bastian Xiii kept his head low all day: on clear days the snipers do not miss.

Bastian Xiii had Pavel Mvuisak of the Concord in his sights at Verdel Ridge for a long second. Pavel Mvuisak was lighting a pipe. Bastian Xiii let the match burn all the way down. Day 3. Verdel Ridge fell to the Concord. Bastian Xiii watched their flag go up on the heights and dug his trench a little deeper.
Bastian Xiii found a clean spot on the table and set his bread on it. Within a minute, someone asked to borrow the spot.

A direct hit on the trench at R-F13. Bastian Xiii was the only one they could still help, and only just. A shell landed square in the trench at R-F13. Bastian Xiii was killed outright. The bearers found nothing to carry.

Hugo Xiii put a rosary of rough beads beside the bunk. Someone who had known Bastian Xiii helped clear the shelf without saying why. First Wave. Hugo Xiii signed when the ink on the posters was still fresh. He keeps the ribbon wrapped in oilcloth with a rosary of rough beads. The new duty roster listed Hugo Xiii as a sniper. He kept checking the old roster until someone took it down.

The blast lifted Hugo Xiii off his feet at R-F13. He came round with a bloody nose and an empty rifle and went back to work. A letter from home found Hugo Xiii before the night shift. Hugo Xiii folded it small and kept it close. Word came down the line: Hill 304 is ours. Hugo Xiii shook hands with a corporal he had never spoken to. Today, everyone was a friend.
Hugo Xiii no longer winces when he lifts his rifle. The medic signed him off with a grunt.
Dawn watch. Hugo Xiii put a round across no man's land and the enemy line went quiet: Bram Satalik, grazed.

Hugo Xiii mended a split glove with pale thread. One finger now looks like it has been promoted. A letter from home found Hugo Xiii before the night shift. Hugo Xiii folded it small and kept it close.
Hugo Xiii caught himself counting portions before counting people. He started again. A letter from home found Hugo Xiii before the night shift. Hugo Xiii folded it small and kept it close.
thswastim05: Edmund Thswastim signed the papers with a steady hand. The trench at Q-F8 took him in like it takes everyone: without a word.
tony2swag_: On Day 9, Edmund Swag arrived during an argument about a missing spoon. The war already had matters more urgent than introductions.
